authority: Cambridge International AS & A Level Physics 9702 syllabus for 2026.
provenance_rule: Every value is tagged syllabus, corpus or judgement. AO names and weights, per-paper splits, paper structure, the Paper 3 mark allocation and the command-word list are transcribed from the syllabus. Frequencies and tariffs are counted from the 12 series examined on the current content (March 2022 to November 2025). The AO roles of command words and the subtype map are our judgement.
evidence_window: March 2022 to November 2025: 12 series, 30 Paper 1s, 30 Paper 2s and 48 Paper 3s with their mark schemes and examiner reports. The 2020-2021 series were mined and set aside: they were set on the syllabus before the current one, and six of their Paper 2s examine electric fields, now A Level content.

assessment_objectives.name: Knowledge and understanding
assessment_objectives.definition: scientific phenomena, facts, laws, definitions, concepts and theories; scientific vocabulary, terminology and conventions (including symbols, quantities and units); scientific instruments and apparatus, including techniques of operation and aspects of safety; scientific quantities and their determination; scientific and technological applications with their social, economic and environmental implications.

assessment_objectives.name: Handling, applying and evaluating information
assessment_objectives.definition: locate, select, organise and present information from a variety of sources; translate information from one form to another; manipulate numerical and other data; use information to identify patterns, report trends and draw conclusions; give reasoned explanations for phenomena, patterns and relationships; make predictions and construct arguments to support hypotheses; make sense of new situations; evaluate hypotheses; demonstrate an awareness of the limitations of physical theories and models; solve problems.

assessment_objectives.name: Experimental skills and investigations
assessment_objectives.definition: plan experiments and investigations; collect, record and present observations, measurements and estimates; analyse and interpret experimental data to reach conclusions; evaluate methods and quality of experimental data, and suggest improvements to experiments.

ao_mark_budget.arithmetic_note: Each paper’s stated AO percentages weighted by the paper’s stated share of the qualification. The syllabus states AO weights as a share of MARKS, so every AO calculation downstream is marks-equivalent, never an item count.

flashcard_subtype_ao_map.tests: A definition, a law or an equation stated precisely, with its symbols and units
The features or properties of something (a particle, a region of the spectrum, a wave)
The difference between two confusable quantities or terms
An ordered sequence: a derivation from definitions, or the steps of an experimental method
The reason for a step or a condition (why many oscillations are timed; why coherence is needed)
An advantage taken to its consequence
A limitation of a procedure, or a source of uncertainty, and what it does to the result
The physics applied to a situation the learner has not met: a qualitative prediction or a design
A change traced to its effect through a relationship (double the extension, four times the energy)
A judgement on data or a method: does the evidence support the relationship, and by what criterion
A calculation with the equation, the substitution, the answer, its unit and a sensible number of significant figures
Reading a graph, a table, a trace or a circuit: a gradient, an area, an intercept, a value
Telling a correct idea from the error it is confused with
Two objectives joined in one problem

flashcard_subtype_ao_map_note: The PERMITTED set per subtype (C-17). Each work-order slot declares a narrower set: Papers 1 and 2 assess only AO1 and AO2, and Paper 3 only AO3 (syllabus page 14), so a topic 1-11 slot never declares AO3 and a topic 12 slot declares only AO3.

blooms_taxonomy.why_both: The assessment objective says what the examination credits. The Bloom level says what the learner is being asked to do. They are different axes and every item carries both.

levels.means: Recall a fact, a term or a list, as stated.
Explain an idea in the learner’s own words, or tell it apart from a neighbouring one.
Use the idea on a case, a figure, a program or a diagram the learner has not been given the answer to.
Break a situation into its parts and trace a cause through to its consequence.
Weigh options against a criterion and reach a justified choice that could have gone the other way.
Build something new from the parts: a design, an algorithm, a plan.

item_mix_target.note: Balance the SUBJECT against this, never a single topic.
